label: homotop
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{homotop}
    Let $M^{2n-1}$ be a dynamically convex contact manifold that admits an exact filling $W$ with vanishing symplectic homology, then $\pi_i(W)=0$ for $i>1$. If $W$ has a finite fundamental group, then $\pi_k(M)=0$ for $1<k<2n-1$.

label: czi
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{czi}
    Let $M^{2n-1}$ be a contact manifold such that it admits an exact filling $W$ with $SH_*=0$. If there exists a non-degenerate contact form $\alpha$ on $M$ with no Reeb orbits of Conley Zehnder index $2+k$ and $1-k$, then $H_{k+n}(\partial W)=0$ and $H_{n-k-1}(\partial W,\mathbb{Z})=0$.
head: environment

label: adc defn
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{adc defn}
    A contact manifold $(M^{2n},\xi)$ with $c_1(M,\mathbb{Q})=0$ is asymptotically dynamically convex if there exists a sequence of contact forms $\alpha_1>\alpha_2>...$ and increasing positive numbers $D_i$ that tends to infinity such that $\mu_{CZ}(\gamma)>3-n$ for any $\gamma $, a non-degenerate Reeb orbits of $\alpha_i$ with action bounded above by $D_i$
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: ADC(Asymptotically dynamically convex) (see definition \ref{adc defn}) contact manifolds were introduced by Lazarev(\cite{lazarev2020contact}) that generalize index positive contact manifolds where one can derive independence of Floer theoretic invariants like positive symplectic homology from its filling. The class of manifolds is rich enough for many applications (for instance see \cite{bowden2022tight},\cite{zhou2021symplectic},\cite{Zhou_2024})

label: zhou
title: Theorem

\label{zhou}

Then for any other topologically simple exact filling $W'$, $\pi_i(M)\rightarrow \pi_i(W')$ is an isomorphism for $i\leq k-2$.

title: Remark
body_md: Symplectic homology $SH_*(W)$ and symplectic cohomology $SH^*(W)$ can also be defined using a Hamiltonian $H$ such that $H$ is quadratic (for instance $r^2$) in the collar $[1,\infty]\times\partial W $ and $C^2$-small in $W$. For such a quadratic Hamiltonian denoted by $H_q$, the homology of the chain complex $SC_*(W,H_q)$ is isomorphic to $SH_*(W)$ defined as the direct limit of linear Hamiltonians. However in order to have a well-defined cochain complex $SC^*(W,H_q)$, it is necessary to use a direct product instead of a direct sum since the differentials are action increasing and the the generators could be infinite. This is not a problem with the definition using linear Hamiltonian because  the differential is a finite sum for action reasons. For more details and a proof of the isomorphism, see \cite{ritter2013topological}.

They coincide with our definition if we define our grading using $-\mu_{CZ}$ instead of $\mu_{CZ}$. He also works with quadratic Hamiltonians. If we want to work  with linear Hamiltonians, it suffices to take the direct limit of $\varinjlim {SH(\Tilde{W},H)}$ induced by lifts of moduli spaces involved in the definition of continuation maps.

label: modulesc
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{modulesc}
    Given a Liouville domain $W$, the pair of pants product makes the symplectic homology of $W$, twisted by $\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1]$ local coefficients a module over $SH_*(\tilde{W})$, the symplectic homology of the universal covering $\tilde{W}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We notice that the chain complex of symplectic homology with $\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1]$ local coefficients is a  subcomplex of that of symplectic homology of the universal cover $SH_*(\tilde{W})$ since its differential coincides with that of $SH_*(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])$ when restricted to finitely many orbits. Now let $\tilde{x}*\tilde{y}$ denote the pair of pants product with an element $\tilde{y}$ represented by an infinite sum of orbits in the fiber of $y$ and a single orbit $\tilde{x}$ in the fiber of $x$ . 

    Let $\mathcal{M}(x,y;z)$ denote the rigid moduli space of pair of pants with incoming ends at $x,y$ and outgoing end at $z$.The unique lifting property holds for a pair of pants $P$ in $\mathcal{M}(x,y;z)$ as $P$ deform retracts to a figure $8$ whose fundamental group is generated by any two boundary components say $x$ and $y$. The image  of the fundamental group of pair of pants by the map $P$, $Im (\pi_1(P))$ is trivial in $\pi_1(W)$ since $x$ and $y$ are contractible. Therefore the lifting lemma implies there is a unique lift of $P$ such that $\tilde{x}$ is a lift of $x$   
    
    
    Let $z$ be an orbit in $W$. The rigid moduli space of pair of pants $\mathcal{M}(x,y;z)$ in $W$ is finite by compactness. Therefore after fixing $\tilde{x}$, there exists only finite lifts of  $\mathcal{M}(x,y;z)$ in $\tilde{W}$. Since the sum of rigid moduli spaces $\Sigma_z\mathcal{M}(x,y;z)$ is finite in $W$, there exists only finite lifts of $\sqcup_z\mathcal{M}(x,y;z)$ having $\tilde{x}$ and $\tilde{y}$ as entries. As a consequence the sum defining $\tilde{x}*\tilde{y}$ is finite implying $\tilde{x}*\tilde{y} \in SH_*({W},\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1(W)])$
     
     Therefore the product $z\in SC(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])$ and we have a module action $SH_*(\tilde{W})\otimes SH_*(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])\rightarrow SH_{*+*-n}(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])$.

title: Corollary

\label{loccoeff}
    Given a Liouville domain $W$, $SH_*(W)=0$ implies $SH_*(W,{\mathbb Z[\pi_1]})=0.$

title: Proof
body_md: Let $\tilde{W}$ be the universal covering of $W$. Since the canonical map $SH_*(W)\rightarrow SH_*(\tilde{W})$ is a unital ring map, $SH_*(W)=0$ implies $SH_*(\tilde{W})=0$. Theorem \ref{module} implies that $SH_*(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])=0$ since the unit of $SH_*(\tilde{W})$ acts as the identity.

title: Theorem

\label{vansc}
    Let $W$ be a Liouville domain such that $SH^*(W)=0$. Then $SH^*(W,k[\pi_1(W)])=0$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The symplectic cohomology $SH^*(W)=0$ implies that the counit $e$ satisfies $e=0$. Since the induced projection $p_*:SH(W,k[\pi_1(W)])\rightarrow SH(W)$ is counital, the lifted counit also satisfies $\tilde{e}=0.$ Therefore  $SH^*(W,k[\pi_1(W)])=0$

label: adualc
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{adualc}
   Given a Liouville domain $W$, $SH_*(\tilde{W},H)\cong Hom(SH^*(W, k[\pi_1]),H,k).$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We can rewrite $SC^*(W,H,k[\pi_1(W)]) $ as $\bigoplus_{x\in \mathcal{P}(H)}\bigoplus_{p(\tilde{x}=x)}k$ where $p:\tilde{W}\rightarrow W$ is the covering projection,by using the identification with the lifted complex of the universal cover. Now applying the $Hom$ functor to this group, we get $Hom(SC^*(W,H),k)\cong \underset{x\in\mathcal{P}(H)}{\bigoplus}\underset{p(\tilde{x})=x}{\Pi}Hom(k,k)$ since the $Hom$ functor sends direct sums to direct products and the first sum is taken over finitely many elements. Therefore we have $Hom(SC^*(W,H),k)\cong SC_*(\tilde{W},k)$ where the latter is the group involved in the definition of symplectic homology of covering space.

    Note that $\tilde{d}(\tilde{x})=\underset{\tilde{y}}{\Sigma}\tilde{\mathcal{M}}({\tilde{x},\tilde{y}})\tilde{y} $ and $\tilde{\delta}(\tilde{y})=\underset{\tilde{x}}{\Sigma}\tilde{\mathcal{M}}({\tilde{x},\tilde{y}})\tilde{x} $ where $\tilde{\mathcal{M}}({\tilde{x},\tilde{y}})$ is the lift of rigid trajectories in $\mathcal{M}(x,y)$ which start from $\tilde{y}$ and end in $\tilde{x}$. Therefore the matrices represented by $\tilde{d}$ and $\tilde{\delta}$ are transpose to each other. Therefore universal coefficients theorem implies that $SH_*(\tilde{W},H)\cong Hom(SH^*(W,H, k[\pi_1]),k)$.

name: "Gluing=Composition"

label: module
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{module}
    The lifted wrapped Floer homology of a covering $\tilde{L}$, $ HW^{(0)}(\tilde{L})$ forms a module over the the wrapped homology of the base $HW(L)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(P,j,\beta)$ be a pair of pants and , then using corollary \ref{gluing=composition} we have $${\Psi}_P(\widetilde{x_1(0)},x_2.x_3)=\Psi_P(\widetilde{x_1(0)},\Psi_{P'}(x_2,x_3))={\Psi}_{P\#_\lambda P'}(x_1(0),x_2,x_3)$$ for $P'$ another model open pair of pants whose negative end can be glued to  the positive end of P. Since the choice of TQFT operations $\Psi_S$ do not depend on $j,\beta,J$, we have proved associativity of the module structure. 
 Note that for  model Riemann surface $E$ with one positive puncture and no negative punctures  induces the TQFT map $$\psi_E:\mathbb{Z}_2\rightarrow HW(L).$$ The unit $e$ is given by  $\psi_E(1)$. Therefore again using the "gluing=composition" lemma \ref{gluing=composition} , we have ${\Psi_P}(\widetilde{x_1(0)},e)={\Psi}_{P\#_\lambda E}(\widetilde{x_1}(0))=\widetilde{x_1}(0).$ The last equality follows since after gluing we get a continuation cylinder at the chain level which corresponds to identity at homology.

label: hom
title: Theorem
body_md: Let $M^{2n-1}$ be a topologically simple dynamically convex contact manifold that admits an exact filling $W$ with vanishing $SH_*(W)$. Then $M$ is a homology sphere.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $k$ be an arbitrary coefficient field. Dynamical convexity implies  $SH_i^+(W,k)=0$ and $SH^i_+(W,k)=0$ for $i<n+1$ and using exactness of the long exact sequence of symplectic homology (Proposition \ref{les}) with the vanishing $SH_*$ assumption forces $H_i(W,\partial W,k)=0$ for $i<2n.$ Moreover $SH_*(W,k)=0$ implies $SH^*(W,k)=0$ by Theorem \ref{adual}. A similar exactness argument using the long exact sequence of symplectic cohomology (Proposition \ref{les2}) implies that $H_i(W,k)=0 $ for $i>0$. The long exact sequence of homology $$...\rightarrow H_i(\partial W,k)\rightarrow H_i(W,k)\rightarrow H_i(W,\partial W)\rightarrow H_{i-1}(\partial W,k)\rightarrow ...$$ implies $\partial W$ is a homology sphere over arbitrary field coefficients. Universal coefficients theorem thereby implies $\partial W$ is a homology sphere over $\mathbb{Z}$ since the homology is finitely generated as $\partial M$ is a compact manifold.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{4.2}
    Let $M^{2n-1}$ be a dynamically convex contact manifold such that there exists an exact filling $W$ of $M$ with $SH_*(W)=0$ and $\pi_1(W)$ is finite. Then, $\pi_k(W)\cong \pi_k(M)$ for $1<k<2n-1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\tilde{W}$ denote the universal covering of $W$.Since $M$ is dynamically convex, $SH_k^+(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])=0$ for $k\leq n$ since there are no generators. The condition $\pi_1(W)$ is finite implies $\tilde{W}$ is compact. After using Lefshetz duality to identify the  cohomology ${H^k}(\tilde{W})$ and $H_{2n-k}(\tilde{W},\partial \tilde{W})$, the canonical long exact sequence with $\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1]$ coefficients is given by

  \[\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
	{...} & {H_{*+n}(\tilde{W},\partial \tilde{W})} & {SH_{*}(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])} & {SH_{*}^{+}(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])} & {H_{*+n-1}(\tilde{W},\partial \tilde{W})} & {...}
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow[from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow[from=1-5, to=1-6]
\end{tikzcd}\] 
    
$SH(W)=0$ implies $SH(W,\mathbb{Z}[\pi_1])=0$ by corollary \ref{loccoeff}.  The long exact sequence implies ${H_{k}(\tilde{W},\partial \tilde{W})}=0$ for $k<2n$. By examining the part $H_1(\tilde{W},\partial \tilde{W}) \rightarrow H_0(\tilde{W})\rightarrow H_0(\partial\tilde{W})$   of the long exact sequence of homology groups, we can conclude that $H_0(\tilde{W})\rightarrow H_0(\partial\tilde{W})$ is injective since $H_1(\tilde{W},\partial \tilde{W})=0$. Therefore injectivity forces $H_0(\partial\tilde{W})=\mathbb{Z}$ since $H_0(\tilde{W})=\mathbb{Z}.$ We conclude that the boundary $\partial\tilde{W}$ is connected. 

      
      Examining the part of long exact sequence of the relative homotopy groups of the pair $(\partial \tilde{W}, \tilde{W}) $ given by  $\rightarrow \pi_1(\tilde{W})\rightarrow\pi_1(\tilde{W},\partial\tilde{W})\rightarrow\pi_0(\partial\tilde{W})\rightarrow \pi_0(\partial W) $, we deduce that $\pi_1(\tilde{W},\partial\tilde{W})=0.$ 

      
 Relative Hurewicz theorem implies ${\pi_{k}(\tilde{W},\partial \tilde{W})}=0$ for $k<2n$. This implies $\pi_k(\tilde{W})\cong \pi_k(\partial \tilde{W})$ for  $k<2n-1$ using the long exact sequence of relative homotopy groups. Since projection from a covering space induces isomorphisms on $\pi_k$ for $k\geq 2$, we get $\pi_k(W)\cong \pi_k(M)$ for $1<k<2n-1$.
head: environment

label: homotopy
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{homotopy}
      Let $M^{2n-1}$ be a dynamically convex contact manifold that admits an exact filling $W$ with vanishing symplectic homology, then $\pi_i(W)=0$ for $i>1$. If $W$ has a finite fundamental group, then $\pi_k(M)=0$ for $1<k<2n-1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $k$ be an arbitrary field. By universal coefficients, we know that $SH_*(W,\mathbb{Z})=0\implies SH_*(W,k)=0.$ The algebraic duality statement \ref{adual} implies $SH^*(W,k)=0.$ This further implies that $SH^*(W,k[\pi_1(W)])=0$ by \ref{vansc}. Now because of dynamical convexity  there are no generators of $SH_+^*(W,k[\pi_1(W)])$ of index less than $n+1$ implying $SH_+^i(W,k[\pi_1(W)])=0$ for $i<n+1$. The long exact sequence \ref{lesloc2} implies that $H_i(\tilde{W},k)=0$ for $i>0$ where $\tilde{W}$ is the universal cover of $W$. 

    Note that $H_i(\tilde{W})$ need not be finitely generated say if $\pi_1(W)$ is infinite. By splitting of the  universal coefficients  short exact sequence we have $H_i(\tilde{W},\mathbb{Z})\otimes k\bigoplus Tor(H_{i-1}(\tilde{W}),k)\cong H_i(\tilde{W},k)$. For $i=1$,we have $H_1(\tilde{W},\mathbb{Z})\otimes k\cong H_1(\tilde{W},k)=0$ since $Tor(\mathbb{Z},k)=0.$ From universal coefficients with $i=2$, we have $Tor(H_1(\tilde{W},\mathbb{Z}),k)=0$. Now $Tor(H_1(\tilde{W},\mathbb{Z}),k)=0$ and $H_1(\tilde{W},\mathbb{Z})\otimes k=0$ implies $H_1(\tilde{W},\mathbb{Z})=0.$ By induction we have $H_i(\tilde{W})=0$ for $i>0$.



For the universal cover $\tilde{W}$, by Hurewicz $\pi_2(W)\cong H_2(\tilde{W})=0$ and by induction $\pi_i(W)\cong0$ for $i>1$. Theorem \ref{4.2} implies that $\pi_i(W)\cong \pi_i(M)$ for $1<i<2n-1$. Therefore we have $\pi_i(M)=0$ for $1<i<2n-1$ since $\pi_i(\tilde{W})\cong \pi_i(W)$ for $i>1$.

title: Remark
body_md: The above proofs can be adapted to working with index bounds that is not necessarily $n+1$ of dynamical convexity. An interesting source of lower bounds on Conley Zehnder index comes from the minimal discrepancy number of the link of a singularity cf \cite{mclean2016reeb}. One can impose restrictions on fillings of its link from the minimal discrepancy number of a singularity.

label: cz
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{cz}
    Let $M^{2n-1}$ be a contact manifold such that it admits an exact filling $W$ with $SH_*=0$. If there exists a non-degenerate contact form $\alpha$ on $M$ with no Reeb orbits of Conley Zehnder index $2+k$ and $1-k$, then $H_{k+n}(\partial W)=0$ and $H_{n-k-1}(\partial W,\mathbb{Z})=0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Our assumption that there exists no Reeb orbit of index $2+k$ and $1-k$ implies that the positive symplectic homology groups $SH^+_{2+k}(W)$ and $SH^+_{1-k}(W)$ vanish since these groups are generated by Reeb orbits of index $2+k$ and $1-k$ respectively. Using the long exact sequence \ref{les} and the fact that $SH_*(W)=0$ we get that $H_{n+k+1}(W,\partial W)=0$ and $H_{n-k}(W,\partial W)=0.$
    
    Working with arbitrary field coefficients $k$, we can similarly get information about $H_*(W,k)$. Absence of Reeb orbits of index $2+k$ and $1-k$ implies that the  positive symplectic cohomology group $SH_+^{2+k}(W,k)$ and $SH_{+}^{1-k}(W,k)$ vanishes. Furthermore vanishing of symplectic homology $SH_*(W,k)$ forces $SH^*(W,k)=0$ by \ref{adual}. Therefore from the exactness of the long exact sequence in symplectic cohomology \ref{les2}, we deduce $H_{n+k}(W,k)$ and $H_{n-k-1}(W,k)=0$ for all field coefficients $k$. Since $W$ is compact , the homology groups $H_*(W,\mathbb{Z})$ are finitely generated. We can conclude using universal coefficients theorem, that $H_{n+k}(W,\mathbb{Z})$ and $H_{n-k-1}(W,\mathbb{Z})=0.$ 

The long exact sequence of relative homology groups of the pair $(W,\partial W)$ is given by \[\begin{tikzcd}
	{...} & {H_{k+n+1}(W,\partial W)} & {H_{k+n}(\partial W)} & {H_{k+n}(W)} & {....}
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow[from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=1-5]
\end{tikzcd}\]. The exactness of the above sequence implies $H_{k+n}(\partial W)=0$ and $H_{n-k-1}(\partial W,\mathbb{Z})=0.$
head: environment

title: Remark

body_md: The theorem \ref{cz} implies that if $H_{k+n}(\partial W)\neq 0$ or $H_{n-k-1}(\partial W,\mathbb{Z})\neq 0$ then there necessarily exists a Reeb orbit of Conley Zehnder index $2+k$ or $1-k$.

label: funda
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{funda}
    Let $L$ be an exact Lagrangian filling with a Maslov zero class of a Legendrian $\Lambda$ in a Liouville domain $W$ with vanishing wrapped Floer homology $HW(L)$. If $\Lambda$ admits a lacunary contact form, then $\pi_1(L)$ is trivial.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The vanishing result of corollary \ref{Vanishing WH} implies that $HW^{(0)}(\tilde{L})=0$ for the universal cover $\tilde{L}$ of $L$. From the long exact sequence \ref{les wcs}, we can conclude that we have an isomorphism ${HW_{n-1}^0}^+(\tilde{L})\cong H^0(\tilde{L}) $. Since we assume that the form is lacunary, the differentials in ${HW_{k}^{(0)}}$ vanish and ${HW_{n-1}^{(0)}}$ is generated by Reeb chords of which there exists at least one since its non-zero. However $H^0(\tilde{L})\cong \mathbb{Z}$ whereas ${HW_{n-1}^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L})={CW^{(0)}_{n+1}}^+(\tilde{L})= \bigoplus_{\mu_{CZ}(x)=n+1}\underset{p(\tilde{x}(0))=x(0)}{\Pi}\mathbb{Z}\tilde{x}(0)\cong \bigoplus_{\mu_{CZ}(x)=n+1}\mathbb{Z}[[\pi_1(L)]]$. Therefore the isomorphism ${HW_{n-1}^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L})\cong H^0(\tilde{L}) $ implies $\pi_1(L)=1$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: In case the filling is not Maslov zero and there exists only one single transverse Reeb chord as in \cite{chantrainefloer}, the above proof works over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ grading. However this is not be the case for the standard Legendrian $\Lambda_{std}$ in $(S^{2n-1},\xi_{std})$, as there are infinitely many Reeb chords for a non-degenerate contact form and the form need not be lacunary. (\cite{kim2024topology},Example 2.6).

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\Lambda$ be a Legendrian in a contact manifold $(Y,\xi)$ such that $c_1(Y,\mathbb{Q})=0$, $\pi_1(Y,\Lambda)=0$ and the Maslov class $\mu_{\Lambda}(Y,\Lambda)$ vanishes. $\Lambda$ is asymptotically dynamically convex if there exists an infinite sequence of contact forms $\alpha_1\geq\alpha_2...$ for $Y$ and an infinite sequence of positive numbers $D_1<D_2<....
$ tending to infinity, such that for any $\gamma\in\mathcal{C}^{>D_i}(\Lambda,\alpha_i)$, $\gamma$ is non-degenerate and index $\mu_{CZ}(\gamma)>1$.

name: Lazarev

label: adcleg
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{adcleg}
    Let $\Lambda$ be an asymptotically dynamically convex Legendrian in an asymptotically dynamically contact manifold $Y$. For two exact Maslov-zero Lagrangians $L_1$ and $L_2$ in Liouville fillings $W_1$ and $W_2$ of $M$, then $HW^+(L_1)\cong HW^+(L_2)$
head: environment

label: adccover
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{adccover}
    Let $\Lambda$ be an asymptotically dynamically convex Legendrian in an asymptotically dynamically convex contact manifold $Y$. For two exact Maslov-zero Lagrangians $L_1$ and $L_2$ in Liouville fillings $W_1$ and $W_2$ of $M$, let  $\tilde{L_1}$ and $\tilde{L_2}$ be covering spaces over $L_1$ and $L_2$ such that $\partial\tilde{L_1}\cong\partial\tilde{L_2}$ as coverings over $\Lambda$. Then ${HW^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L_0})\cong {HW^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L_1})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The proof of proposition \ref{adcleg} follows by proving that the assumptions imply  the differential in $HW^+(L_i)$ is defined using  moduli spaces that  do not enter the Liouville filling by a neck stretching argument. In this setting, let $u\in\mathcal{M}_0(x,y)$ be a rigid trajectory between Reeb chords which do not enter the filling. Then $\alpha_0(u)$ defines the same path in $[1,\infty]\times \Lambda$ whether it is seen in the completion of  $L_1$ or in the completion of $L_2$. Therefore after fixing a lift $\tilde{x}_0$ of $x(0)$, $\alpha_0(u)$ lifts to the same path in the cylindrical ends of $\tilde{L_1}$ and $\tilde{L_2}$ by uniqueness of lifting. Therefore the differentials coincide in ${HW^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L_0})$ and ${HW^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L_1})$ implying ${HW^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L_0})\cong {HW^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L_1})$.

label: funda1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{funda1}
        Let $W^{2n}$ be a Liouville filling of $(S^{2n-1},\xi_{std})$ with $n>2$  and let $L$ be an exact Lagrangian filling of the standard Legendrian $\Lambda_{std}$ with vanishing Maslov class. Then $\pi_1(L)=1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The Lagrangian $L$ is proven to be spin in \cite{kim2024topology},section 2.3.1. Therefore we can work with wrapped Floer theory with $\mathbb{Z}$ coefficients. By \cite{chantrainefloer} we know that for an exact Maslov zero Lagrangian filling $L_1$ of $\Lambda_{std}$ in the standard ball $D^{2n}$,  $\pi_1(L_1)=1$. Therefore the positive wrapped Floer homology group of the universal cover $${HW^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L_1})\cong HW^+(L_1).$$  Since $HW(D^{n}_{std})=0$, the long exact sequence \ref{les wcs} in wrapped Floer homology implies $${HW_{n-1}^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L_1})\cong HW_{n-1}^+(L_1)\cong H^0(L_1)\cong\mathbb{Z}$$  
    
    Now considering the Liouville filling $W$, note that the map $\pi_1(\Lambda)\rightarrow\pi_1(L)$ induced by inclusion is injective since $\pi_1(\Lambda_{std})=0$. Therefore the the boundary $\partial\tilde{L}$ of the universal cover $\tilde{L}$ is given by $\pi_1(L)/\pi_1(\Lambda)=\pi_1(L)$ copies of $\Lambda_{std}$. Therefore  $\mathcal{L}:=L_1\times \pi_1(L)$ is a cover over $L_1\subset D^{2n}_{std}$ such that $\partial \mathcal{L}=\Lambda_{std}\times\pi_1(L)$, coinciding with $\partial \tilde{L}$.  
    
    The Legendrian $\Lambda_{std}$ and $(S^{2n-1},\xi_{std})$ are asymptotically dynamically convex and they satisfy the assumptions of proposition \ref{adccover}. Hence by proposition \ref{adccover} $$ {HW_{n-1}^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L})\cong {HW_{n-1}^{(0)}}^+(\mathcal{L})=\Pi_{\pi_1(L)}HW_{n-1}(L_1)\cong\Pi_{\pi_1(L)}\mathbb{Z} $$
    The long exact sequence of the wrapped Floer homology of the universal cover $\tilde{L}$ (proposition \ref{les wcs}) implies $ H^0(\tilde{L})\cong {HW_{n-1}^{(0)}}^+(\tilde{L}) $. Since $H^0(\tilde{L})=\mathbb{Z}$, we have $\mathbb{Z}\cong\Pi_{\pi_1(L)}\mathbb{Z}.$ This implies $\pi_1(L)=1$.
head: environment

label: lagrangian filling proof
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{lagrangian filling proof}
    Let $W^{2n}$ be a Liouville filling of $(S^{2n-1},\xi_{std})$  and let $L$ be an exact Lagrangian filling of the standard Legendrian $\Lambda_{std}$ with vanishing Maslov class. Then $L$ is diffeomorphic to the ball $B^n$ for $n\neq 1,2,4$ and homeomorphic to $B^n$ when $n=4$ .
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For a Maslov zero exact Lagrangian filling, $\pi_1(L)=0$ by theorem \ref{funda1} for $n>2$. For Maslov-zero exact fillings, $H_i(L,\partial L)\cong H_i(B_n,\partial B_n)$ by theorem A in \cite{kim2024topology}. Therefore by h-cobordism theorem, $L$ is diffeomorphic to the ball $B^n$ when $n\geq 6$. . The $n=3$ case is implied by Perelman's proof of the Poincare conjecture. When $n=4$, $L$ is homeomorphic to $B^4$ by Friedman's theorem\cite{freedman1982topology}. The proof of smooth Poincare conjecture for smooth homotopy $5-$spheres (\cite{kervaire1963groups}) implies the $n=5$ case. The $n=2$ case follows after noticing that that $(S^3,\xi_{std})$ has a unique Liouville filling by the standard ball and then applying the Eliashberg-Polterovich theorem (\cite{eliashberg1996local}) on uniqueness of exact Lagrangian filling.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Let $W$ be a topologically simple Liouville filling of a contact manifold $M$ that have vanishing symplectic homology and nice enough Reeb dynamics (for instance lacunary) on $M$. We can infer $\pi_1(W)=0$ using symplectic homology of covering spaces in a similar fashion to the proofs in the  Lagrangian setting of theorem \ref{funda}.

label: zhouprop
title: Proposition
body_md: \label{zhouprop} Let $M$ be an ADC-contact manifold and $W$ be a topologically simple exact filling of $M$ . Then for the universal covering $\tilde{W}\rightarrow W$ the map $\tilde{\partial_\delta}:H_{*+n+1}(\partial \tilde{W},k)\rightarrow SH^{-*}_+(\partial {W},k[\pi_1(W)])$ is independent of topologically simple exact filling $W'$ and covering $\tilde{W'}$ as long as $\partial\tilde{W}=\partial\tilde{W'}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Note that Zhou uses grading by $-\mu_{CZ}$ and therefore follows a cohomological convention for symplectic homology.Symplectic cohomology in \cite{zhou2021symplectic} is equivalent to the construction of symplectic homology in this paper.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Note that Zhou (\cite{zhou2021symplectic}) uses a quadratic Hamiltonian to define symplectic homology. Therefore to have a well defined differential in symplectic cohomology using a quadratic Hamiltonian, we must replace the direct sum in  $SC(W,H,J):=\bigoplus _{\gamma\in \mathcal{P}(H)}{\mathbb{Z}}\gamma$ by a direct product $SC(W,H,J):=\Pi _{\gamma\in \mathcal{P}(H)}{\mathbb{Z}}\gamma$. We could also stick to a direct sum construction and replace $SH^k$ by an action bounded version (see remark \ref{action bound}). One could also try to adapt Zhou's proof to linear Hamiltonians.

label: zh
title: Theorem
body_md: Let $M$ be an ADC contact manifold with a topologically simple exact filling $W$ such that $SH_*(W)=0$ and $\pi_i(M)\rightarrow \pi_i(W)$ is an isomorphism for $i=1,2$. Then for any other topologically simple exact filling $W'$, $\pi_i(M)\rightarrow \pi_i(W')$ is an isomorphism for $i=1,2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $i=1$, $\pi_1(M)\rightarrow \pi_1(W')$ is an isomorphism by \cite{zhou2021symplectic}(Theorem E). Therefore for the universal cover $\tilde{W'}$ of $W'$ and universal cover $\tilde{M}$ of $M$ we have $\partial \tilde{W'}=\tilde{M}$. Therefore by proposition \ref{zhouprop}, the map $\tilde{\partial_\delta}:\partial_\delta:H_{*+n+1}(\partial \tilde{W'},k)\rightarrow SH^{-*}_+(\partial {W'},k[\pi_1(W)])$ is independent for topologically simple exact filling $W'$. 
   
    Since symplectic homology vanishes, so does symplectic cohomology $SH^*(M,k)$ by proposition \ref{adual} and so does symplectic cohomology of the universal cover $SH^{-*}_+(\partial {W},k[\pi_1(W)])$ by theorem \ref{vansc}. This implies by proposition \ref{lesloc2},that $H_{*+n+1}(\tilde{W'})\cong SH^{-*}_+(\partial W',k[\pi_1(W')])$. We can make the identification $\pi_2(M)\cong H_2(\tilde{M})$ and $\pi_2(W)\cong H_2(\tilde{W})$ since the second homology of universal cover is isomorphic to $\pi_2$ by Hurewicz theorem and since $\pi_2(\tilde{X})\cong \pi_2(X)$ for any space $X $ and its covering $\tilde{X}$. Therefore $H_2(\tilde{M},k)\cong H_2(\tilde{W},k)$ by universal coefficients theorem applied to $H_2(\tilde{M},
    \mathbb{Z})\cong H_2(\tilde{W},\mathbb{Z})$. By proposition \ref{zhouprop}, $H_2(\tilde{M},k)\cong H_2(\tilde{W'},k)$ for all topologically simple Liouville fillings . Universal coefficients theorem and the structure theorem for finitely generated abelian groups implies $H_2(\tilde{M})\cong H_2(\tilde{W})$. The previous isomorphism  is a  verification by first comparing the ranks of the two group followed by iteratively checking $\mathbb{Z}_{p^m}$ part in their decomposition using the properties $Tor(\mathbb{Z}_n,\mathbb{Z}_m)\cong \mathbb{Z}_m\otimes\mathbb{Z}_n\cong\mathbb{Z}_{gcd(m,n)}$.After identifying these groups with $\pi_2$, we have $\pi_2(M)\cong\pi_2(W')$.

label: higherhomproof
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{higherhomproof}
    Let $M$ be an ADC contact manifold with a topologically simple exact filling $W$ such that $SH_*(W)=0$ and $\pi_i(M)\rightarrow \pi_i(W)$ is an isomorphism for $i\leq k$. Then for any other topologically simple exact filling $W'$, $\pi_i(M)\rightarrow \pi_i(W')$ is an isomorphism for $i\leq k-2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof of cases till $k=4$ is implied by theorem \ref{zhou}. The hypothesis $\pi_i(M)\rightarrow \pi_i(W)$ for $i\leq k$ implies $\pi_i(W,M)=0$ for $i\leq k$. Using relative Hurewicz theorem on the universal covers $\tilde{W}$ and $\tilde{M}$ so that one doesn't have to factor out by an action of $\pi_1(M)$ , we have $H_i(\tilde{W},\tilde{M})=0$ for $i\leq k$. Now the long exact sequence of homology groups of the pair $(\tilde{W},\tilde{M})$ implies $H_i(\tilde{M})\rightarrow H_i(\tilde{W})$ is an isomorphism for $i\leq k-1$
  
    As in the proof of theorem \ref{zhou}, using proposition \ref{zhouprop} we get $H_i(\tilde{M})\cong H_i(\tilde{W'})$ for $i\leq k-1$. By the long exact sequence of relative homology groups, this implies $H_i(\tilde{W'},\tilde{M})=0$ for $i\leq k-1$
    and thereby  $\pi_i(\tilde{W'},\tilde{M})=0$ for $i\leq k-1$ by relative Hurewicz theorem. The long exact sequence of homotopy groups now implies $\pi_i(\tilde{M})\cong \pi_i(\tilde{W'})$ for $i\leq k-2$. Since $\pi_i(\tilde{X})\cong\pi_i(X)$ for $i>1$, for any space $X$ and its universal cover $\tilde{X}$. We can conclude $\pi_i({M})\cong \pi_i({W'})$ for $i\leq k-2$.
